user.title: Add a GitHub token
user.description:
Private Repositories installs and updates custom integrations from GitHub repositories, private ones included. It needs a fine-grained token that can read them.

1. On GitHub, open the [new fine-grained token]({new_token_url}) page.
2. **Resource owner**: your account, or the organization that owns the repositories.
3. **Expiration**: up to one year. Home Assistant reminds you before it ends.
4. **Repository access**: *Only select repositories*, then the repositories to track.
5. **Permissions**: *Repository permissions* › **Contents**: *Read-only*. Nothing else.
6. Generate the token, copy it and paste it below.

An organization may have to approve the token before it works. The token stays in Home Assistant and is only sent to GitHub's API.

data_description.access_token: A fine-grained personal access token, starting with github_pat_.

reauth_confirm.title: Replace the GitHub token
reauth_confirm.description:
GitHub no longer accepts the token of {account}: it expired or was revoked.

Open [your tokens]({tokens_url}) on GitHub, open the token, choose **Regenerate token** and a new expiration, then copy the new token and paste it below. If the token no longer exists, create a [new token]({new_token_url}) with **Contents**: *Read-only* on the same repositories.

data_description.access_token: A fine-grained personal access token, starting with github_pat_.

reconfigure.title: Replace the GitHub token
reconfigure.description:
Paste a new token for {account}. It must belong to the same GitHub account and read the same repositories.

To renew the current token, open [your tokens]({tokens_url}) on GitHub, open the token and choose **Regenerate token**. To start over, create a [new token]({new_token_url}).

user.title: Add a repository
user.description:
Pick a repository the token can read, or type `owner/name`. Updates follow its GitHub releases.

If its integration is not installed yet, its latest release is installed right away, and a repair offers to restart Home Assistant to load it.

data_description.repository: The repository holding the integration, as owner/name.
data_description.prereleases: Also offer releases marked as pre-releases on GitHub.

adopt.title: Take over {integration}
adopt.description:
The integration `{integration}` {version} is already installed, but not from `{repository}`. From now on, its updates will come from the releases of `{repository}`.

If another tool such as HACS manages it, remove it there first: one integration should be updated by one tool only.

data_description.prereleases: Also offer releases marked as pre-releases on GitHub.

progress.install:
Downloading and checking the latest release of `{repository}`, then installing its integration.

You can close this dialog: the install goes on, and the repository is tracked once its integration is installed. An integration that is already installed is only taken over once you confirm it here.

renew.title: Renew the GitHub token
renew.description:
The token of {account} expires on {date}. After that, updates stop.

1. Open [your tokens]({tokens_url}) on GitHub, then this token.
2. Choose **Regenerate token** and a new expiration (up to one year).
3. Copy the new token and paste it below.

Its repositories and permissions stay the same. To start over instead, create a [new token]({new_token_url}) with **Contents**: *Read-only* on the same repositories.
